title: 5 February 2010. Siri was an app on the App Store before Apple owned it.
description:
Siri was an app on the App Store before Apple owned it. It arrived as a third party app for the iPhone, from a company that had spun out of SRI.

It grew out of a government funded AI project. MIT Technology Review says it was built on artificial intelligence research done at SRI as part of the CALO project.

Co-founder and chief executive of Siri. He told eWeek the app would reach Android and BlackBerry phones within months.

Apple bought it within three months of launch. The deal surfaced in an FTC filing dated 27 April 2010. Xconomy later gave a reported price of US$150 million to US$250 million.

Analysts did not expect Android or BlackBerry versions after the sale. eWeek thought it doubtful Siri would ever reach them. MIT Technology Review called a Siri for Android an unlikely prospect.

Siri came back inside the iPhone 4S. Apple launched the phone with a beta version of Siri. After the announcement it removed the standalone app from the App Store.

Once Apple built it into the iPhone, it pulled the original app.

Sources:
- https://legacy.xconomy.com/?p=158552: read (Wade Roush, around the iPhone 4S launch; the date is inferred from its content, not stated). Established that Siri was introduced as a third party app for the iPhone 3G on 5 February 2010; that Apple bought the company in April 2010 for a reported US$150 million to US$250 million; and that Siri had won US$24 million in funding from Menlo Ventures and Morgenthaler Ventures.
- https://www.eweek.com/news/apple-buys-siri-a-small-victory-in-mobile-web-war-with-google/: read (28 April 2010, Clint Boulton). Established that Siri launched its first app into the App Store in February; that the purchase surfaced from an FTC filing dated 27 April 2010 which gave no further information; that Dag Kittlaus was co-founder and chief executive; that Kittlaus said Siri aimed to reach Android and Research In Motion phones in the coming months; and that the writer thought it doubtful Siri would ever reach Android or BlackBerry.
- https://www.technologyreview.com/2010/04/29/204026/apple-expected-to-acquire-siri/: read (29 April 2010, Erica Naone). Established that the purchase was reported and not confirmed, that Siri was built on artificial intelligence research done at SRI as part of the CALO project, and that a Siri for Android was now an unlikely prospect.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siri: read. Established that Siri is a spin-off from SRI International's AI Center and an offshoot of the DARPA funded CALO project; that on 14 October 2011 Apple launched the iPhone 4S with a beta version of Siri; and that after the announcement Apple removed the standalone Siri app from the App Store.
